role_note: test-reviewer, round 6. One question per test: would it fail if the code were wrong? Every claim below was MEASURED by mutating sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/FaultInjectingStore.java, deleting sequencer/build/test-results/test, running ./gradlew :sequencer:test --tests 'binjava.sequencer.FaultInjectingStore*' --rerun-tasks --no-build-cache, then reverting with git checkout --. 40 mutants run; every one reverted and verified clean. Scope kept to FaultInjectingStore and its two test classes; the five untracked M4.19/M4.20 files were not read or run.
method: Baseline: 15 tests green (FaultInjectingStoreTest 10, FaultInjectingStoreStreamsTest 5, counted from the JUnit XML). Each of the 15 was shown to uniquely kill at least one mutant, so none is decoration. Two surviving mutations were additionally quantified with a throwaway probe test (created, run, deleted) so the finding is measured rather than argued.

findings.title: putIfMatch's draw ORDER is unpinned: the two alignment-only draws can be MOVED below the ambiguous throw and the whole suite stays green
findings.surviving_mutations: MEASURED, mutant M7. In putIfMatch I moved `fires(unreachableDraws, ...)` and `fires(duplicateDraws, ...)` from above the `if (ambiguous)` block to below it (so a firing ambiguousPut skips them) and left everything else identical. ALL 15 TESTS PASSED. Round 5's fix closed DELETION of those two statements (M5: delete the unreachable draw -> killed by everyClassDrawsOnEVERYFaultingCall; M6: delete the duplicate draw -> killed) but not REPOSITIONING, because that test runs with Faults.none() so the ambiguous branch is never taken, and aFIRINGClassDoesNotSHIFTTheStreamsOfTheClassesAfterIt drives putIfAbsent only (its own comment says so). Quantified with a probe: a workload alternating putIfAbsent and putIfMatch, unreachable=0.05, recording the call indexes where the unreachable class fired, run with ambiguousPut=0 then 0.5. Correct code: positions MOVED in 0 of 40 seeds. M7 mutant: MOVED in 39 of 40 seeds (seed 0: [60] -> [30,44,60,82]; seed 1: [28,30,50,102,106,112] -> [38,42,72]).
findings.failure_scenario: putIfMatch is the lease's only CAS and M4.13 is scheduled to edit exactly these three statements ('putIfMatch gets ambiguousPut but never unreachable, so a lease CAS cannot fail cleanly ... M4.13 owns closing this'). Two of them are result-discarding calls that read as dead code -- the round-5 W1 finding said as much -- so the natural tidy-up is to push them down next to the code that would use them, or below the guard clause. That is M7, and it silently re-opens the regression the backlog row says was shipped three times: a class that fires shifts the streams of the classes after it, so criterion 1's 'hold the seed, toggle one class, attribute the difference' becomes unobtainable on the lease path. The row claims this commit covers 'per-class stream independence in BOTH halves (the scrambler as a function AND the draw order through the store)'; the second half holds for putIfAbsent only.
findings.what_would_close_it: One assertion, deterministic and cheap: a second store at Faults(0, 1.0, 0), one putIfMatch that DOES fire ambiguousPut (catch the IOException), then assert drawCounts() equals {unreachable=1, ambiguousPut=1, duplicatePut=1}. Correct code gives 1/1/1; M7 gives 0/1/0. Alternatively extend aFIRINGClassDoesNotSHIFT's workload to interleave putIfMatch, which is what the probe above did and which kills M7 on 39 of 40 seeds.

findings.title: eachClassIsWIREDToItsOWNStream pins the wiring of putIfAbsent's three draws only; the read verbs' and putIfMatch's draws can be wired to ANY stream with the suite green
findings.surviving_mutations: MEASURED, two mutants. (a) M36: `stat` changed to `fires(duplicateDraws, faults.unreachable())` -- the unreachable class drawing the duplicatePut class's stream. ALL 15 TESTS PASSED. Probe: record duplicatePut's fault positions over 120 putIfAbsent calls at duplicatePut=0.05, once with 0 preceding stat() calls and once with 7. Correct code: positions MOVED in 0 of 40 seeds. M36: MOVED in 40 of 40 (seed 0: [57,63,94,97,115] -> [50,56,87,90,108]). (b) M40: in putIfMatch, swapped which Random the ambiguous decision and the discarded duplicate draw take (`fires(duplicateDraws, faults.ambiguousPut())` / `fires(ambiguousDraws, faults.duplicatePut())`). ALL 15 TESTS PASSED -- the count test cannot see it because each stream is still drawn exactly once, and the putIfMatch ambiguity test runs at p=1.0 so it fires whichever coin it holds. The new wiring test drives putIfAbsent only (callsWhereOnly at line 135), so 4 of the 5 faulting sites are unconstrained as to WHICH class's stream they consume.
findings.failure_scenario: The test's name promises the general property ('each class is wired to its own stream and not aliased onto another's') while constraining one verb, which is the coverage-claimed-by-prose failure this task keeps recording. The concrete trigger is scheduled: M4.13 adds fault injection to put, getRange, multipart and delete and makes putIfMatch fail cleanly, i.e. it adds new `fires(...)` call sites by copying existing ones -- the single most likely place for a wrong field name, and nothing would notice. The consequence is the same cross-class aliasing the wiring test exists to forbid: reads are what recover's chain walk does, so under M36 every recovery read consumes the duplicatePut class's stream and that class's positions become a function of how many reads happened, destroying the per-class attribution criterion 1 rests on.
findings.what_would_close_it: Same one test as V1, extended: after the four conditional writes in everyClassDrawsOnEVERYFaultingCall, add store.stat(..), store.get(..) (catching) and store.list(..) and assert drawCounts() == {unreachable=7, ambiguousPut=4, duplicatePut=4}. The read verbs then have an ASYMMETRIC expected count, which is what makes wiring visible: M36 gives {unreachable=6, duplicatePut=5} and dies. Add the fired-putIfMatch case from V1 and M40 dies too. One test, both findings.

findings.title: drawCounts() counts fires() INVOCATIONS, not stream consumption, and the instrument the alignment property now rests on is itself unverified
findings.surviving_mutations: MEASURED, three mutants, all SURVIVED all 15 tests. M32: an extra `draws.nextDouble()` inside fires -- each stream is consumed 8 times while drawCounts still reports 4, so the javadoc 'how many times each class's stream has been drawn' is false and unfalsifiable. M35: `if (p == 0.0) return false;` after countDraw -- counted but NOT drawn, which is verbatim the lazy-draw shape the fires javadoc at :128-131 says it exists to prevent. M37: countDraw's own ternary relabelled so ambiguousDraws reports 'duplicatePut' and duplicateDraws reports 'ambiguousPut' -- the count test cannot see it because it asserts a map whose ambiguousPut and duplicatePut values are both 4, so the instrument's per-class attribution is unconstrained by construction.
findings.failure_scenario: The test asserts a structural mirror of the code (three fires calls per conditional write => 4/4/4) rather than a behaviour, so it breaks on any refactor that adds a fault class or shares draws between verbs, and it passes if the counter lies. Someone reading 'four conditional writes, so every class drew exactly four times' will believe the streams were consumed in step when only the call sites were counted. It does earn its keep -- it is the sole killer of the shared-Random mutant and of both putIfMatch draw deletions -- so this is a limits-of-the-instrument note, not a request to remove it; but the javadoc on drawCounts should say it counts call sites, and the map should be made asymmetric (see V2) so that at least the unreachable class's attribution is checkable.
findings.what_would_close_it: Rename/redocument drawCounts as counting faulting call sites per class, and make the expected map asymmetric so the labels are discriminated. M35 additionally dies if fires is asserted to consume the stream even at p=0 -- e.g. two stores at the same seed, one at Faults.none() and one at Faults(0,0,1.0), driven the same number of calls, must agree on the duplicatePut positions of a THIRD store; simpler is to accept that with one Random per class the p==0 early return is behaviour-neutral and say so instead of claiming otherwise in the javadoc.

findings.title: Split residue: three Javadoc comments left behind, now attached to unrelated @Test methods and describing helpers that live in the other file
findings.surviving_mutations: Not a mutation finding -- a false-coverage claim in prose. :179 ('Whether stream {@code stream} for {@code seed} fires on its {@code draw}-th draw') is the Javadoc of firesAt, which is now FaultInjectingStoreStreamsTest:86; as written it documents aProbabilityOUTSIDEZeroToOne. :241-250 ('Drives a fixed call sequence and records which call index EACH class fired on ... attribution is by the growth of injected()') documents firedIndexesWith, now StreamsTest:188; as written it documents theREADSideFaultsToo. :296-302 ('The call indexes at which kind fired, with only its own class enabled ... p = 0.9 ... which is what makes isNotEqualTo a real discriminator') documents callsWhereOnly, now StreamsTest:127; as written it documents EVERYClassRecordsWHICHKeyItFaultedOnTheWritePathToo. Also `import java.util.ArrayList;` at :16 is now unused.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader (or the next reviewer) reads the p=0.9 aliasing rationale sitting directly above EVERYClassRecordsWHICHKey and concludes that test pins the stream wiring. It pins keys. This project's recorded failure mode is exactly a row or comment asserting coverage that lives somewhere else -- and here it asserts coverage that lives in a different file, which is harder to check, not easier.
findings.what_would_close_it: Delete the three orphaned comments and the unused import; the text they carry already exists on the helpers in FaultInjectingStoreStreamsTest.

findings.title: body(String) is duplicated verbatim in both halves of the split
findings.surviving_mutations: Not a mutation finding. The two copies are byte-identical today.
findings.failure_scenario: The fixture is the thing that decides whether a Body can be opened once or twice -- the property FaultInjectingStore's ambiguous path depends on, since it read()s the body and re-wraps it. When someone tightens body() to a single-shot InputStream to pin strict streaming (the memory-flatness work already does this elsewhere), they will tighten one copy, the other file will keep testing the lenient shape, and the two halves of one property will disagree with no test failing.
findings.what_would_close_it: One package-private fixture helper in the sequencer test package, used by both.

findings.title: The pure pass-through verbs are driven by no test at all (T5 from round 5, still open)
findings.surviving_mutations: MEASURED, four mutants, all SURVIVED all 15 tests. M28: `delegate.getRange(k, b, a)` -- the range bounds swapped. M29: delete(keys) made a no-op. M30: close() made a no-op (the delegate is never closed). M34: put() returning null instead of delegating.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.13 owns adding injection to put, getRange, multipart and delete. It will add code to four methods that currently have no test driving them at all, so the first version of that injection -- including whether it records an Injected at all -- lands unconstrained; and today a decorator that silently stops delegating a range read or a delete would be found by the simulation as a protocol violation rather than as a broken harness.
findings.what_would_close_it: One test per verb through CountingBinStore or MemoryBinStore asserting the call reached the delegate with the same arguments. Cheap, and it gives M4.13 a place to add the fault assertions.

findings.title: The row says 'the decorator and TWELVE unit tests'; the staged tests are FIFTEEN
findings.surviving_mutations: Not a mutation finding. Counted from the JUnit XML of a clean --rerun-tasks run: FaultInjectingStoreTest tests="10", FaultInjectingStoreStreamsTest tests="5".
findings.failure_scenario: The row itself says this sentence 'has now been wrong twice -- "six" while nine were staged, then nine while twelve were'. It is now wrong a third time, in the same commit that says so, and backlog.md is what milestone-review reads at M4's completion condition. The row already contains the right answer in the next sentence ('A COUNT IN PROSE GOES STALE ... so what matters is WHAT is covered'); the count should simply go.
findings.what_would_close_it: Delete the number and keep the list of what is covered -- with 'the draw order through the store' narrowed to putIfAbsent until V1 and V2 are closed, since as written that clause is measurably broader than the tests.

questions_the_task_asked.is_drawCounts_behaviour_or_implementatio: Implementation, and knowingly so -- see V3. It counts fires() call sites, not stream consumption (M32/M35 survive), and its expected map is symmetric so it cannot attribute a label (M37 survives). It nevertheless earns its keep: it is the ONLY killer of the shared-Random mutant (M1) and of both putIfMatch draw deletions (M5, M6), and I measured that no toggle comparison can reach those, so I am not asking for its removal. Raised as minor.
questions_the_task_asked.is_the_wiring_test_flaky_or_deterministi: Deterministic. Seed 3 is fixed, p is fixed, java.util.Random is a specified LCG, and no clock or global RNG is touched -- the fired-index lists are a fixed computation with a fixed answer, so it can be permanently wrong but it cannot flake. Coincidental equality of two independent 60-call lists at p=0.9 is (0.9^2+0.1^2)^60 ~ 8e-6, and p=0.9 is the right choice for the opposite reason the comment gives credit for: an ALIASED stream produces an exactly IDENTICAL list (verified -- M2, M3 and M4 all die on isNotEqualTo), so the discriminator is identity, not similarity. One correction to its comment: the one-shared-Random-OBJECT mutation (M1) is NOT killed by this test -- three fires calls per verb interleave on one stream, so the three lists still differ -- it is killed by everyClassDrawsOnEVERYFaultingCall. The comment at :98-102 credits this test with catching it.
questions_the_task_asked.does_the_split_leave_either_class_incohe: FaultInjectingStoreStreamsTest is coherent -- five randomness properties, no assertion about what a fault does to a caller. FaultInjectingStoreTest carries three orphaned Javadoc comments and one unused import (V4), which is the only incoherence, and body(...) is duplicated (V5). The seam itself is real and I would not move it back.
questions_the_task_asked.do_the_ten_remaining_tests_still_constra: Yes, and each was measured, not assumed. anAmbiguousPutLANDS kills M17 (landing deleted); aDuplicatedPutIsHarmless kills M16 (re-PUT via put, clobbering the winner); aStoreConfiguredWithNoFaults kills M9 (fires always true); anInjectedFaultCHANGES kills M10 (fires always false); anAmbiguousPutIfMatchALSOLands kills M18 (putIfMatch landing deleted); aProbabilityOUTSIDE kills M13 (guard body disabled) and M14 (naive p<0||p>1, which accepts NaN); aDUPLICATEDPutREALLYREACHES kills M15 (re-PUT deleted) and M21 (duplicate key blanked); theREADSideFaultsToo kills M23 (stat's kind relabelled), M24 (get's key blanked) and M25 (list's record dropped); theInjectedRecordIsASNAPSHOT kills M26 (List.copyOf -> live list); EVERYClassRecordsWHICHKey kills M19, M20 and M22 (unreachable/ambiguous keys blanked on putIfAbsent and putIfMatch). No assertion in the staged files is weaker than what these mutants require, and both new files are additions, so there is no existing assertion to have been loosened.

previous_round_findings.T1_wiring_unconstrained: CLOSED. eachClassIsWIREDToItsOWNStreamAndNotAliasedOntoAnothers kills all three: M2 (all three fields seeded from stream 1 as distinct objects), M3 (alias 3->1), M4 (alias 2->3). M1 (one shared Random OBJECT) is also killed, by the count test rather than by this one -- see the correction under questions_the_task_asked.
previous_round_findings.T2_draw_order_one_stream_one_verb: PARTIALLY CLOSED, residue re-raised as V1 and broadened as V2. Closed: the counting half (M5 and M6, putIfMatch's two discarded draws deleted, both die on everyClassDrawsOnEVERYFaultingCall) and the attribution rewrite (M8c, putIfAbsent's ambiguous+duplicate draws made lazy, dies on the rewritten aFIRINGClassDoesNotSHIFT -- so attributing by growth of injected() rather than by the caught exception is a real improvement and now covers duplicatePut, which no exception could reach). Not closed: on putIfMatch the draws can be MOVED below the throw (M7) and can be wired to the wrong stream (M40), and on the read verbs the stream is unconstrained (M36).
previous_round_findings.T3_write_path_key_unpinned: CLOSED. EVERYClassRecordsWHICHKeyItFaultedOnTheWritePathToo kills M19 (putIfAbsent unreachable key blanked), M20 (putIfAbsent ambiguousPut key blanked) and M22 (putIfMatch ambiguousPut key blanked). With the pre-existing read-verb and duplicatePut coverage, all six Injected sites now have both kind and key pinned -- I checked each site individually.
previous_round_findings.T4_fires_internals: NOT CLOSED, and I am not re-raising it as major, because I measured the three mutants and judge two of them behaviour-equivalent for every property this file claims. M33 (`<` -> `<=`) differs only when nextDouble() returns exactly 0.0 while p == 0, i.e. one run in 2^53. M31 (nextDouble -> nextFloat) changes WHICH seeds fire but breaks neither independence (each class still owns its Random) nor alignment (one draw per class per call either way). M32 (an extra draw per fires) is the one with real content, and it is folded into V3 as the reason drawCounts' javadoc is unfalsifiable. If the author wants these pinned, one golden assertion -- the exact fired-index list for a named seed at a named p -- closes all three at once, and would also pin the stream numbers 1/2/3 that the decorrelation test currently supplies as literals.
previous_round_findings.T5_read_and_lifecycle_verbs: NOT CLOSED, re-recorded as V6 with the same severity it had (minor). M28 getRange bounds swapped, M29 delete no-op, M30 close no-op and M34 put returning null all still survive, because no test drives those four verbs at all.

what_is_strong: The three fault classes are pinned on the property that matters rather than on their existence: the ambiguous write is asserted to LAND on both putIfAbsent and putIfMatch and the duplicate is asserted to REACH the delegate twice through CountingBinStore, with the pre-owned-key fixture that makes putIfAbsent-vs-put distinguishable -- an earlier draft that could not tell them apart is called out in the test's own comment. aStoreConfiguredWithNoFaults and anInjectedFaultCHANGESWhatTheCommitLogDoes are a real negative control and a real outcome-difference assertion rather than a fires-count. The NaN case in the probability guard is the right case to pick, and it kills the naive rewrite. And the two new streams tests are the first thing in six rounds to make the per-class independence property falsifiable at all: the decorrelation test kills seed*3+stream on statistics that are a fixed computation rather than a sample, and the wiring test kills all three aliasings on exact list identity.
process_note_not_a_test_finding: Two majors at round 6 against review.md rule 12's two-round cap. I record honestly that they are majors -- both are measured surviving mutations on the property the backlog row claims this commit covers, and M4.13 is scheduled to edit the exact statements they leave unpinned -- but I also record that they are ONE test change, not a split: extending everyClassDrawsOnEVERYFaultingCallSoNoClassCanBeSKIPPEDSilently with three read verbs and one fired putIfMatch kills M7, M36 and M40 together. The commit is not too big; the streams properties were simply all asserted through one verb.
